A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NoiseSDF2NoiseSDF study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across formatting changes and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original reconstruction experiments on ShapeNet, ABC, Famous and Real, together with supervision, architecture, training-strategy and noise ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative comparisons, a multi-target ablation, simulated LiDAR corruption results and complex-shape visual examples.

M1.justification: Appendix A.3.2 introduces a 1-to-3 variant that averages SDF predictions from three independently corrupted target clouds instead of using one target. The principal pairwise method, frozen Point2SDF generator, MSE objective and inference procedure remain unchanged; Appendix A.5 supplies architecture details without establishing an architecture revision.

E1.justification: The named datasets and surface-reconstruction task remain unchanged. Appendix A.3.3 adds a distinct simulated LiDAR sensing scenario on ShapeNet Chair, incorporating depth-dependent noise, irregular sampling, dropout and outliers beyond the previously tested additive noise distributions.

E2.justification: V3 substantially expands the evaluated alternatives: Neural-Singular-Hessian and Poisson reconstruction across the six ABC/Famous/Real conditions in Table A.9, IterativePFN followed by 3DS2V on Chair in Table A.10, and LaGeM in the complex-shape comparison of Figure A.6. Earlier comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Existing splits, training budgets, point counts and metrics remain unchanged. New experiments introduce three LiDAR corruption levels evaluated with CD/F1 and Chair comparisons at Gaussian noise 0.01 using a two-stage pipeline and three-target supervision. Numerical parameters defining the LiDAR severity levels are not provided.

E4.justification: V3 retains the earlier ablations and adds several substantive analyses: whether separate point denoising followed by reconstruction suffices, whether multiple noisy targets improve training and reconstruction, robustness to structured LiDAR corruption, and complex-geometry visual cases. These address additional questions beyond redisplaying existing benchmark results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. V3's qualitative statement about more stable multi-target training does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All eight original tables retain their numerical values after matching renumbering. Tables A.9–A.12 and Figure A.6 add substantial results: high-severity LiDAR F1 is 0.518 for 3DS2V versus 0.601 for Ours, while 1-to-3 IoU is 0.923 versus 0.927 for 1-to-1. Table A.9 also reports Ours' Famous 0.02 Chamfer as 0.034, conflicting with the retained 0.032 in Tables 3–4.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.4 add a mathematical analysis absent from v2: a local normal-projection model, zero-mean Gaussian perturbations, and a first-order derivation of approximately unbiased signed distances, including at the zero level set. This supplies new theoretical reasoning for a simplified local model; the earlier loss and metric formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claim of learning clean neural SDFs through noisy supervision are unchanged. V3's contribution list and revised conclusion elevate robustness across noise types, target generators and denoising backbones to an explicit main claim, broadening the conclusion's earlier emphasis on noise levels 0.01 and 0.02.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly acknowledges substantial training requirements and dependence on target-generator quality, and warns that misleadingly clean reconstructions can be problematic in medical applications. V2's speculative NeRF extension and energy-saving claims are removed. Interpretations of the retained benchmark results remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 newly documents farthest-point sampling, 512 anchors/latent tokens, 24 self-attention layers and attention inputs. Conversely, v3 removes Section 8 and Appendix I.5's statements about a supplementary code ZIP, preprocessing scripts, README and planned public repository. This establishes changed reproducibility documentation, without establishing whether external code availability changed.

R1.justification: V3 adds Neural-Singular-Hessian to related work, cites IterativePFN for the new pipeline, and adds Hong et al. and Du et al. in the introduction. The ImageNet-initialization citation is removed. The central novelty positioning relative to image Noise2Noise and point-cloud methods is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include contribution bullets, reordered ablation subsections, localized wording edits, an expanded conclusion, reorganized end matter and appendices, and revised author/header and citation formatting.

P2.justification: V3 substantially reformats the main text and references from one column to two, resizes and relocates existing displays, and reorders Tables 6–8. It adds four appendix tables, a complex-shape figure and an architecture diagram. The earlier appendix visualization is retained as Figure A.5.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens scrutiny of the retained central results through additional baselines, multi-target and structured-noise tests, first-order theoretical reasoning, and explicit limitations. These provide useful evidence and clearer applicability boundaries. The gains are tempered by removal of code-access documentation, unspecified numerical LiDAR corruption settings, and the new Famous Chamfer discrepancy between Table A.9 and Tables 3–4.
